questions.question: What is the sum of interior angles of a pentagon?
questions.explanation: Sum of interior angles = (n - 2) × 180°, where n = number of sides. For pentagon (n = 5): (5 - 2) × 180° = 3 × 180° = 540°.

questions.question: If a polygon has 8 sides, what is the sum of its interior angles?
A regular polygon has each interior angle measuring 135°. How many sides does it have?
questions.explanation: For regular n-gon: each interior angle = (n - 2) × 180° / n. So 135 = (n - 2) × 180 / n. Solve: 135n = 180n - 360. -45n = -360. n = 8.
questions.fastStrategy: Interior angle of regular polygon = (n - 2) × 180° / n.

questions.question: Two supplementary angles have measures in the ratio 2:3. What are their measures?
questions.explanation: Supplementary angles sum to 180°. Ratio 2:3 means 2x + 3x = 180. 5x = 180. x = 36. Angles: 2(36) = 72°, 3(36) = 108°.
questions.fastStrategy: Supplementary angles sum to 180°; use ratio to set up proportion.

questions.question: A line intersects two parallel lines. If one alternate interior angle measures 65°, what is the other alternate interior angle?
questions.explanation: When a transversal intersects parallel lines, alternate interior angles are equal. Both measure 65°.
questions.fastStrategy: Parallel lines + transversal: alternate interior angles are equal.
